pharm: Anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and antipyretic; relatively COX-2 selective
summary: Nimesulide is a sulfonanilide NSAID with preferential COX-2 inhibition, used as a second-line agent for acute pain and primary dysmenorrhea. Following an EMA safety review, use is restricted to short courses of no more than 15 days at 100 mg twice daily because of the risk of serious, sometimes fatal, hepatotoxicity. It is contraindicated in any hepatic impairment, with alcohol, and in children under 12 years.

dosage.n: After food; max 200 mg/day; limit to ≤15 days; second-line only
After food; max 200 mg/day; limit to ≤15 days; second-line only
Not for use in children under 12 years

admin: Take orally after food to reduce GI upset
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration
Do not exceed 200 mg per day or a 15-day treatment course
Stop immediately at the first sign of liver injury
moa: Preferentially inhibits cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), reducing prostaglandin synthesis at sites of inflammation, which produces anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and antipyretic effects with relatively lower COX-1 (gastric) inhibition.

absolute: History of hepatotoxic reaction to nimesulide
Any hepatic impairment or active liver disease
Active or recurrent peptic ulcer or GI bleeding
Fever or flu-like symptoms (risk of masking)
relative: Cardiac, renal, or mild hepatic risk factors

preg: Avoid throughout pregnancy, especially late gestation; contraindicated in the third trimester (risk of premature ductus arteriosus closure and oligohydramnios/renal effects).
lact: Contraindicated / not recommended; no safety data available during breastfeeding.
renal: Contraindicated in severe renal impairment; use with caution in mild-to-moderate impairment with monitoring of renal function.
hepatic: Contraindicated in any hepatic impairment or active liver disease. Stop immediately if signs of liver injury occur (anorexia, nausea, jaundice, dark urine, right-upper-quadrant pain, raised transaminases).

major: Other NSAIDs or aspirin (additive GI and renal toxicity)
moderate: ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and diuretics (renal injury, reduced effect)
interactions.alcohol: Contraindicated due to increased hepatotoxicity risk.

serious: Hepatotoxicity (acute hepatitis, cholestasis, fulminant hepatic failure leading to transplant or death)

monitoring: Liver function tests at baseline and if symptoms develop
counsel: Take after food and only for up to 15 days
Stop and seek care if you develop anorexia, nausea, vomiting, fatigue, dark urine, jaundice, or right-upper-quadrant pain
Strictly avoid alcohol while taking this medicine
Do not use with other NSAIDs or hepatotoxic drugs
Report any liver symptoms to your doctor immediately
pk: Below 25–30°C, protect from moisture and light
pearls: EMA restricted nimesulide to second-line, short-term (≤15 days) use for acute pain and dysmenorrhea due to hepatotoxicity
Withdrawn or banned for children and chronic use in several countries
Idiosyncratic liver injury is the defining safety concern—stop at the first hepatic warning sign
Never combine with alcohol or other hepatotoxins
missed: Take when remembered unless it is near the next dose, in which case skip it. Do not double the dose. Do not extend treatment beyond 15 days.
overdose: Symptoms include nausea, vomiting, epigastric pain, drowsiness, and lethargy; possible GI bleeding, hypertension, acute renal failure, hepatic dysfunction, and rarely respiratory depression or coma. Management is supportive: activated charcoal within 1–2 h, monitor hepatic and renal function; there is no specific antidote, and dialysis is unlikely to help due to high protein binding.
